repo_notes.content: nix-os is the NixOS configuration of TWO small, live VPSs, one flake with a system per host, both on nixos-26.05: `piabrota` (Hostinger KVM 1: 1 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 50 GB disk; hostname srv2108887) serves www.piabrota.art, the public web; `piabrota2` (Hostinger KVM 4; measured on 2026-11-04: 4 vCPU, 15.6 GiB RAM, 196.8 GiB disk) runs Hermes Agent, its dashboard on hermes.piabrota.art and PGX. The systems are nixosConfigurations.piabrota and nixosConfigurations.piabrota2, built by mkHost from hosts/<name>/default.nix, which imports configuration.nix (what both hosts share) and adds the host's own name and roles. It is not a library or a template for many machines, though docs/FORK.md explains how to fork it for another VPS.

A merge to main IS the deploy: .github/workflows/deploy.yml builds both systems on a GitHub runner (job `build`, which saves the Nix store in GitHub's Actions cache) and deploy-rs copies each one over SSH as the `deploy` user and switches its VPS (job `deploy`, a matrix with one job per host; a host whose address secret is not set is skipped, not failed). If SSH does not answer within 60 seconds after the switch, or a unit fails during activation, deploy-rs rolls that VPS back ('magic rollback'). The VPSs never compile. Changes to Markdown only do not deploy. When a deploy fails, .github/workflows/deploy-doctor.yml runs piabrota/agents' deploy-doctor on a GitHub runner; nothing of piabrota/agents runs on the boxes.

AGENTS.md is the source of truth for rules: the file table, 'Do not break the machine' (settings that keep the VPS reachable: qemu guest agent, cloud-init, OpenSSH, GRUB on /dev/sda, the deploy user, magic rollback; never change system.stateVersion), the resource budget, and the rules for commits and PRs. Prefer its wording when documenting rules.

Resource budget: every change is judged by what it adds to the system closure (measured with dix) and to resident memory. No GUI, fonts or desktop services; no heavy runtimes for small jobs; no resident daemons the host does not need. The rules hold on both hosts: piabrota2 has room for the full Hermes, not for heavy tools on every host, and a tool that only one host needs goes in that host's directory. tools.nix removes the NixOS manual and caps the journal; deploy.nix sets garbage collection and keeps five boot generations.

The repository's own modules use the option namespace piabrota.*: piabrota.site (site.nix), piabrota.loco.apps.<name> (loco.nix), piabrota.pgx (pgx.nix), piabrota.hermesWeb (hermes-web.nix), piabrota.lofi (lofi.nix, the Discord music bot in lofi/). configuration.nix imports the modules that every host shares (site, loco, pgx, lofi, kubesolo-purge.nix); each host turns on its own roles: piabrota turns on piabrota.site and imports apps.nix; piabrota2 imports hermes.nix (services.hermes-agent, the upstream module from the flake input hermes-agent), hermes-github.nix and hermes-web.nix, and turns on piabrota.hermesWeb, piabrota.pgx and piabrota.lofi.

Secrets never live in the repository (it is public). They are files on the box written by hand: /var/lib/loco-secrets/<app>.env for Loco apps, /var/lib/hermes-secrets/hermes.env for Hermes Agent (copied into its .env at activation), and PGX's generated password. Units read them with EnvironmentFile or systemd LoadCredential. Document where a secret lives and how it is written, never a value.

kubesolo-purge.nix is a temporary oneshot that clears, once, what an old install left on the box (pods, mounts, /var/lib/kubesolo, cni0, KUBE- and CNI- rules); it runs only while /var/lib/kubesolo exists and a human deletes it in a later PR.

Hermes Agent (github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent, Nous Research) runs on the host piabrota2 as the unit hermes-agent from its flake's NixOS module (hermes.nix): native mode, not a container; pinned to the release v0.23.1 (commit 3b421578588243f920886e6fe79a6faa87ea026e, 2026-11-09) by tag in flake.nix and by commit in flake.lock; the full package (upstream's default) plus the anthropic, messaging, mcp and ddgs extras; MemoryMax 8G and CPUWeight 50 (hosts/piabrota2/default.nix); state in /var/lib/hermes. Measured at rest on 2026-11-04: hermes-agent about 0.4 GiB. Its web dashboard is the unit hermes-backend (hermes-web.nix, MemoryMax 2G) on 127.0.0.1:9119 behind nginx at hermes.piabrota.art with TLS and basic auth; h0ffmann runs the CLI with `sudo -u hermes hermes ...` and is not in the hermes group. Two Claude models on the owner's subscription (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, never an API key) and no fallback provider: claude-sonnet-5-5 is the main model, claude-haiku-5-5 takes the subagents (read-only fan-out only, at most 2, one level deep) and three side tasks (titles, skill matching, the /goal judge). goals.max_turns is 6 and agent.max_turns 60. A deploy that changes its settings, environment, skills, plugins or documents reloads the unit (reloadTriggers): SIGUSR1 drains the turns in flight for at most 600 s (agent.restart_after_turn_timeout), the gateway exits 75 and Restart=always starts it with the new config; a new package restarts it at once. hermes-github.nix gives it write access as the GitHub App piabrota-hermes[bot] (hermes/* branches and PRs only, humans merge). Upstream calls Nix a best-effort Tier 2 platform, so flake.nix pins the input to a release tag and a bump is a PR by hand; the weekly flake-update PR does not move it. www.piabrota.art/hermes shows its configuration as YAML, built by site/hermes.nix from the evaluated system with every secret-named key dropped. See docs/HERMES.md, docs/MIGRATION-KVM4.md (the move from KVM 1 to KVM 4) and the wiki pages wiki/Hermes-EN.md and wiki/Hermes.md.

PGX (pgx.dev) is a Postgres-compatible engine in Rust used for data that can be lost; it runs on piabrota2 (MemoryMax 256M, about 0.1 GiB at rest on 2026-11-04), nothing uses it, and it stays for the next workload that needs Postgres. Apps keep their own data in SQLite: no PostgreSQL server or Redis for an app.

Documentation is bilingual: pt-BR first with an English mirror (docs/X.ptBR.md and docs/X.md; wiki/ pages Home, Arquitetura, Operacao, Hermes, Maquetes with Home-EN, Architecture, Operations, Hermes-EN, Mockups). Mirrors change together. This DeepWiki should be written in English and may cite either language's file.

Figures and drawings are generated, never hand-edited: archify figures from docs/archify/*.json (just figure), the homepage mockups from mockups/*.nix (just mockups), the README drawing from drawings/mu.nix (just drawing). CI fails when a committed output is stale.
Dates in the docs are real (the repository was built in late October 2026). Measurements carry their date; numbers marked with a warning sign were not measured on the machine.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: What nix-os is: two live VPSs as one flake (piabrota, KVM 1, serves the public web; piabrota2, KVM 4, runs Hermes, its dashboard and PGX), what each serves, how a merge becomes a deploy, the machines' sizes, and where to start reading (README.md, AGENTS.md).

pages.title: Two hosts and the move to KVM 4
pages.purpose: How one flake builds two systems: hosts/<name>/default.nix (hosts/piabrota and hosts/piabrota2: the host name, the roles, piabrota2's Hermes limits), configuration.nix (what both hosts share), the mkHost and mkNode helpers in flake.nix, the deploy matrix in .github/workflows/deploy.yml and freeze.yml (one job per host, skipped when the address secret is missing), docs/MIGRATION-KVM4.md (the checklist that moved Hermes, its GitHub App, its dashboard and PGX from KVM 1 to KVM 4), hermes-web.nix (the dashboard behind nginx, TLS and basic auth at hermes.piabrota.art) and the /hosts page of the site, which shows what each VPS does.

pages.title: The flake and its modules
pages.purpose: flake.nix's outputs (nixosConfigurations for each host, deploy, checks, packages, devShells) and configuration.nix with the modules it imports, the piabrota.* options each defines, and how they fit together.

pages.title: Users, tools and the resource budget
pages.purpose: piabrota.nix (the h0ffmann user, SSH key only, flakes) and tools.nix (the CLI tools, documentation removed, journald caps, zram), and the resource budget rules in AGENTS.md: closure size, dix, no GUI, no heavy runtimes.

pages.title: Do not break the machine
pages.purpose: The settings that keep the VPS reachable and provisionable by Hostinger (qemu guest agent with its PATH, cloud-init, OpenSSH, GRUB, the deploy user, magic rollback, stateVersion), why each exists, and how to undo a bad switch.

pages.title: Deploying
pages.purpose: deploy.yml's build job and its deploy job (one matrix job per host), deploy-rs and magic rollback, the Nix store cache, deploy.nix (the deploy user, five boot generations, the weekly nix.gc of paths older than 14 days, min-free 2 GiB and max-free 8 GiB instead of a garbage collection on each deploy, the weekly store optimisation), the secrets the workflow uses, and docs/DEPLOY.md's one-time setup.

pages.title: CI and checks
pages.purpose: ci.yml (on PRs: nixpkgs-fmt, statix, deadnix, shellcheck, figure-check, the justfile parse; nix flake check by hand only), the justfile's recipes, the flake's checks (both systems, deploy-rs, loco-example, the pgx VM test, mockups, drawing), cves.yml, freeze.yml and the scripts in scripts/.

pages.title: The site
pages.purpose: site.nix and site/: the Gleam and Lustre site prerendered at build time, its three designs from mockups/data.nix (with the human and agent commit counts of each own repository, refreshed by scripts/commit_counts.py), the /hermes page (Hermes's configuration as YAML from site/hermes.nix, with no secret), the /hosts page (what each of the two VPSs does), nginx with ACME, the www redirect, the skills.piabrota.art vhost (skills-site/) with the 301 from /skills, site/DESIGN.md's look, and design/ (the design kit: tokens, CSS modules, design/sites.nix, and the brand bar for pages from other repositories, with the indexes of proof-site/; docs/DESIGN-KIT.md).

pages.title: Mockups, figures and drawings
pages.purpose: mockups/ (SVG in pure Nix), the archify figures (docs/archify, vendor/archify, just figure) and drawings/ (the mu drawing from Desmos equations), and the CI checks that keep their outputs in sync.

pages.title: Loco apps
pages.purpose: loco.nix's piabrota.loco.apps option (a sandboxed unit per app, SQLite, nightly backups, nginx on a domain or a path), apps.nix and the notes demo in apps/notes, and docs/LOCO.md: adding an app, secrets on the box, growing SQLite.

pages.title: PGX
pages.purpose: pgx.nix and pgx/: the release packaged with autoPatchelfHook, the pgx unit (on piabrota2) and its sandbox, pg_hba.conf for loopback only, the pgx CLI wrapper, the VM test, and docs/PGX.md's cost and limits.

pages.title: Metrics page
pages.purpose: metrics.nix, metrics/collect.sh, metrics/pull.sh, metrics/index.html, metrics/SCHEMA.md, metrics/test/, metrics/test.nix and docs/METRICS.md: the home-made metrics page at metrics.piabrota.art on piabrota2 (static page, nginx with ACME, public with a robots.txt and agent blocks, and an optional basic-auth login), the POSIX sh collector run by a 10 s timer on both hosts (reads /proc and cgroups only), the KVM 1 data path (an allow-listed /_metrics/piabrota.json location pulled by metrics-pull), the offline rules, the measured cost, the hardening, the piabrota.metrics options, the tests and the preview.

pages.title: OpenRig
pages.purpose: openrig.nix, openrig/, docs/OPENRIG.md, docs/RUNTIMES.md, docs/REELS.md, reels/, wiki/Reels-EN.md, hermes/skills/hermes-rig/references/reels-fabric.md and unfree.nix: OpenRig 0.7.7 built from source with buildNpmPackage, the openrig unit on piabrota2 (loopback only, MemoryMax 2G for the daemon, tmux and every seat), the seats' omp (omp/wrapper.nix with no ceiling) and the root step that gives them the Claude subscription token as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, the Claude Code seats of the port rig (unfree.nix allows claude-code by name; seatClaude moves the token to CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json holds their deny rules), a comparison of every OpenRig runtime, the rig wrapper and deny rules for Hermes, and the RigSpecs and AgentSpecs in openrig/specs, installed at /etc/openrig/specs: piabrota-dev, the block wave-forecaster-dev (two rigs that port WW3 to Rust in h0ffmann/chaceon, with a read-only GitHub token and an outbox for Hermes; the oneshot unit and timer openrig-wf-keeper, option waveForecaster.alwaysOn, restore the stopped port rig every 2 minutes, skip when another rig runs and leave a rig that rig down stopped) and reels-fabric (a film crew of five seats in one pod, crew: creative director, producer-editor, 3D artist, music director and QA, with the owner as executive producer, that make a 15 s or 30 s Instagram reel with Claude only; the screenplay hash gate; the toolkit reel in reels/ with its fonts; the options piabrota.openrig.reels.enable and piabrota.openrig.reels.blender.enable (Blender headless, Cycles on the CPU, the owner's exception to no GUI), both off; five phases of two seats; the outbox /var/lib/rig-outbox/reels-fabric).

pages.title: Hermes Agent
pages.purpose: hermes.nix, hermes-web.nix, docs/HERMES.md, docs/MIGRATION-KVM4.md and wiki/Hermes-EN.md: what Hermes Agent is here and that it runs on piabrota2, the upstream NixOS module from the flake input hermes-agent (pinned to the release v0.23.1), the env file on the box and how activation copies it (where each secret lives, never a value), SOUL.md and hermes/AGENTS.md, the skills (hermes/skills/, hermes-manim among them), the manim package for it (pkgs.manim with two tests disabled, on piabrota2 only), MCP servers and the deny-list plugin, hermes-github.nix's GitHub App, the dashboard (hermes-web.nix: hermes-backend behind nginx, TLS and basic auth), the move from KVM 1, checking it, updating and turning it off.

pages.title: Hermes runtime and deploys
pages.purpose: How the hermes-agent unit runs and restarts on piabrota2: native mode, the full package (upstream's default) and its extras, MemoryMax=8G and CPUWeight=50 (hosts/piabrota2/default.nix), the dashboard unit hermes-backend with MemoryMax=2G, /var/lib/hermes, the time zone; what activation rewrites on a deploy (config.yaml, .env, SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, plugin links), the reloadTriggers and ExecReload with SIGUSR1, the drain of turns, cron jobs and subagents for at most agent.restart_after_turn_timeout (600 s), exit code 75 and Restart=always, the immediate restart on a new package, and how to check that a deploy took effect.

pages.title: Hermes models and run limits
pages.purpose: The two Claude models on the subscription and why: claude-sonnet-5-5 as the main model (planning, writing, review, compression, approvals), claude-haiku-5-5 for read-only subagent fan-out and the auxiliary tasks (title_generation, skills_hub, goal_judge); no fallback providers; the delegation limits; agent.max_turns 60, goals.max_turns 6 for /goal, tool-loop hard stop, the memory and disk limits (agent cache, cron, kernels, inbound media, session pruning) and what is turned off (update checks, model catalog, telemetry, lazy installs). Point to www.piabrota.art/hermes for the full YAML.

pages.title: The deploy doctor
pages.purpose: .github/workflows/deploy-doctor.yml: when deploy fails, piabrota/agents' deploy-doctor runs on a GitHub runner from an image pinned by digest, as the GitHub App piabrota-ops, and reports the failure; its secrets (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, OPS_BOT_APP_ID, OPS_BOT_KEY).

pages.title: Working on this repository
pages.purpose: AGENTS.md's rules for people and agents: branches, pull requests in English only, no agent trail and its one exception, never deploying by hand, never committing secrets, the justfiles that must run on Ubuntu 24.04's just, the bilingual docs and the wiki workflow.

pages.title: Forking for your own VPS
pages.purpose: docs/FORK.md: what to change in a fork, the manual steps on Hostinger and GitHub, and the first deploy.

pages.title: Claude and MCP setup
pages.purpose: .agents/skills (the vendored skills and their licences), .mcp.json (mcp-nixos, OpenPencil, DeepWiki) and docs/CLAUDE_PROJECT.md.

pages.title: The thesis rig
pages.purpose: openrig/specs/rigs/wave-forecaster-thesis, openrig/specs/agents/thesis-*, thesis/ and docs/THESIS.md: six Claude Code seats (editor, librarian, three writers, reviewer; only the librarian has the web) write one UFRJ Escola Politécnica final-year project in pt-BR, one independent section at a time, and the command `thesis` (POSIX sh, jq, awk, pandoc, pdfLaTeX; no model, no network) does the mechanical work: thesis fetch claims a section with an atomic file, submit runs lint, build-section, cite-check, slop and readability, verdict records a sha256 of the accepted text, assemble and publish build and hand over the PDF to /var/lib/rig-outbox/wave-forecaster-thesis. Covers the project tree (thesis.json, sections, sources, refs.bib, REFERENCES.md, state, claims, review, build), the template (h0ffmann/forecast-energy-demand pinned by commit, an overlay for the UFRJ front pages, the ABNT author-date CSL instead of coppe.bst, the Lua filter, raw TeX off, the template interface for a second template such as CoppeTeX), the four gates and what each cannot prove (slop is a local heuristic, not a detector), the UFRJ rules (Resolução 05/2012 in force, Norma 2026 a proposal), the option piabrota.openrig.thesis.enable (off), and the deployment notes. No seat has run the rig; the proved part is the toolkit on a sample thesis.
